One step per CAUSE of Roast reds, measured by the cao's census (scrip m3 and rakudo unfudged per red program), each cure proven on a scratch worktree by a base-against-cure differential before it is written here.

column7: X1: a double-quoted string whose whole body is ONE interpolated part ("$x", "$!", "@a[]", "%h<k>", "{ ... }") is a Str, as Rakudo stringifies it: today lower_interp_str in src/parsers/raku/rk_tree.c returns the interpolated node itself when no literal text surrounds it, so "$e" ~~ Str is False, "$!".WHAT is the exception class and "$!" ~~ /boom/ dies error 241 (pattern match left operand is not a string). CURE: at the end of lower_interp_str, after the last literal flush and before the return, when result is non-null and is neither TT_CAT nor TT_QLIT, replace it with expr_binary(TT_CAT, leaf_sval(TT_QLIT, ""), result). MEASURED by the cao on a scratch worktree (SCRIP 52f53c466 + the one line): witness red on the base, green on the cure in m3; base-against-cure over 339 roast programs (the 103 that contain a lone interpolation plus the 257 PASS programs): see the row LEDGER for the gains and that no PASS is lost.

X2: a colon pair whose value is in angle brackets (:lang, :x) is a NAMED argument of a call, as :x(...) already is: named_form in src/parsers/raku/rk_tree.c accepts TK_CP with ck v and cnt P only, so :x (cnt W) is built as a bare positional "y" (sub g(*@a, *%h) receives [1, "y"] and {}; f(:lang

, 1) binds "P" to $a). With :lang named, EVAL must take it: a call EVAL(src, :lang) is then built as __rk_named_call("EVAL", ...), which no EVAL arm in lower_raku.c sees, so the lowerer turns that named call back into the EVAL call with the lang value as a second argument, and bt___rk_eval throws for any language but Raku: X::CompUnit::UnsatisfiedDependency for Perl5 (Rakudo: Could not find Inline::Perl5), X::Eval::NoSuchLang "No compiler available for language 'L'" otherwise; both classes registered in rk_exc_init beside X::Cannot::Empty (without the registration the throw crashes in rk_exc_message: SIGSEGV, the cao measured it). The S01-perl-5-integration programs guard with try { EVAL("1", :lang) } and skip-rest: today EVAL succeeds and they run Perl 5 code. DEPENDS ON STEP 1: S29-context/eval test 14 reads "$!" ~~ /rt112472/, which dies error 241 until step 1 lands, losing tests 15-18. MEASURED on a scratch worktree (52f53c466 + this step): witness green m3; base-against-cure over the 126 roast programs that pass a colon pair with an angle value: ten S01 programs PASS (rc 0, every test ok), advent2013-day10 +3 ok, S06-signature/unspecified +2, S12-methods/chaining +1, S06-signature/types SIGSEGV becomes an honest short run, S29-context/eval -4 (step 1 cures it); every other program unchanged.
